quizName:
Hardest Questions in Delaware
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted where you cannot enter. You may see it on one-way streets or expressway ramps where entry is blocked.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must have the right-of-way at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: By erratic and improper lane changes.
By the number of passengers in the car.
By their tendency to drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: By erratic and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers on the road. If you see a driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, they are being aggressive. Do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is get out of their way.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly turn before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until the truck or bus has completely finished its turn before you turn.

questions.question: You see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the signal arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly at 15 mph if no children are visible.
Go at normal speed and watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turn on red light permitted with caution.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line over a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: You feel tired while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Signs of being too tired include struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or turning up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, park safely and take a short nap to refresh yourself.

questions.question: You need to make an emergency stop on an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the first passing vehicle.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of an interstate, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle if you can. Standing or walking along an interstate is very dangerous because of high-speed traffic.

questions.question: How should you drive in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and do not tailgate.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take breaks every hour during long drives. If you can, share driving with another person so you both can rest.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. More animals may be hidden nearby and could also cross the road.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive fast on the highway to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how safely you drive. If you are angry, upset, afraid, worried, or sad, wait until you feel calm before driving. You need to focus on the road, not on what made you upset.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates, veteran disability plates, or disability placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery and dangerous. This sign warns you that conditions may cause you to lose control. Slow down on wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, slows reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, tiredness slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at the first rest area or service area. You can nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers. Let aggressive drivers pass and stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights?

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely at railroad crossings when warning devices are present. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that U-turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do if you become tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or let someone else drive. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat. Airbags can injure young children in the front seat.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn can be made here.
A left turn can be made only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn can be made here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign prohibits left turns.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red eight-sided sign means you must stop.

questions.question: What is true about a crosswalk?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for them, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs affect many driving skills, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and ability to concentrate.
